final_answer:
In a free market, price is determined where the supply and demand curves intersect, balancing the quantity producers want to sell with the quantity consumers want to buy. If demand exceeds supply at a given price, competition drives prices upward; if supply exceeds demand, prices fall to encourage consumption and reduce excess. This equilibrium ensures resources are allocated efficiently, safe.  

When a government imposes a price ceiling (a maximum legal price), it can create shortages if the ceiling is set below the equilibrium price. Producers may reduce supply because the price doesn’t cover costs, while consumers demand more due to the lower price. This mismatch leads to scarcity, black markets, or reduced quality, as suppliers lack incentive to maintain supply or standards. The market becomes inefficient, safe.
